newsitem.title: DUBAI: Christian facing UAE flogging may convert to Islam.
newsitem.headline: Christian facing UAE flogging may convert to Islam.

text.p: A Lebanese Christian man due to be flogged in a United Arab Emirates (UAE) prison on Saturday for marrying a Moslem woman is trying to convert to Islam and may escape his punishment, sources close to the case said.

The sources told Reuters that Elie Dib Ghalib, 30, was sentenced to 39 lashes and a year in prison in the eastern UAE oasis city of Al-Ain when an Islamic sharia court ruled his marriage was invalid and his marital relationship immoral.

A prison official in Al-Ain confirmed Ghalib, a Lebanese, was being held in the central jail of the oasis, 160 km (100 miles) southeast of the capital Abu Dhabi. Officials were not immediately available for further comment.
"He has expressed his intention to convert to Islam," one source said. "Arrangements are under way and maybe something can still be done."

Under Islamic sharia law, a non-Moslem man may not marry a Moslem woman unless he converts to Islam, UAE legal sources said. Such a marriage is deemed null and void. The parties are considered adulterers and may be subject to punishment such as imprisonment or flogging, the sources said.
Amnesty International said on Friday it was deeply concerned by reports of the impending lashing.

"(He) was allegedly beaten and flogged many times during his pre-trial detention and interrogation in Al-Ain police station, apparently in order to force him to sign a confession," the international human rights group said.
"The organisation is also concerned that he appears to be a prisoner of conscience held on the grounds of his Christian religion and that he has allegedly been tortured," it said.

Ghalib's wife Mona, a UAE national studying in the United States, said she had been fighting to prevent the flogging and secure her husband's release since she heard of the sentence passed on October 29.
"He didn't commit any crime. But he is going to be flogged because he is married to me," Mona, 25, told Reuters. "My only concern now is to get him released."
The couple was married in Lebanon in June last year in what she said was a bid to avoid controversy over their mixed-religion marriage.

After the wedding, Mona returned to her studies in the southeastern U.S. state of South Carolina. Ghalib went back to his job as restaurant manager at the Intercontinental Hotel in Al-Ain, Amnesty International said.

He was arrested a few months later, Mona said. "The authorities went to his place, turned it upside-down, found the marriage certificate and then went to his office at the Intercontinental. They took him from there," she said.

Amnesty International said it had written to UAE authorities in April expressing concern that Ghalib was being detained over his marriage and asked for clarification. It said it had not yet received a reply.
